mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, measured by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and thus a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when controlling for inflation (t-test p > 0.05) during high demand periods.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment, proxied by PAYEMS, reduces labor market uncertainty and boosts investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next month.
failure_condition: Monthly forward returns are negative despite rising PAYEMS, indicating labor strength does not translate to equity optimism in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in FEDFUNDS turns positive (signaling tightening), short-term rates are expected to rise, reducing the present value of future earnings and pushing S&P 500 60-day forward returns negative.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS tightening, suggesting other offsetting factors dominate.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening demand or supply constraints, lowering growth expectations and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite INDPRO declines, implying supply shock is not the dominant factor.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) erode real earnings, triggering a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate profit compression.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative after controlling for inflation expectations (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals a labor market softening, which typically precedes equity market corrections and results in negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when UNRATE remains above 5% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) and rising federal funds (FEDFUNDS) creates a contradictory inflation risk premium, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as markets price expectations of a sharp policy response.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change < -0.5% while FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.1%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the interaction effect rank IC < 0.05 over the 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent industrial production declines (INDPRO) and rising labor costs (PAYEMS), firms face margin compression, leading to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate earnings stagnation.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite continued INDPRO declines and rising PAYEMS, indicating other offsetting factors are dominant.
